sovereign_country.strategic_role: 亚太高客单价数字内容、游戏出海与本土电商合规

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Distribution of Virgin Polyethylene and Polypropylene Granules

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement Between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (entered into force 1 December 2007)
Free Trade Agreement Between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America (KORUS FTA)
Free Trade Agreement Between the Republic of Korea and the European Union and its Member States
Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes Between States and Nationals of Other States (ICSID Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Specific Financial Information Act, Act No. 5491, as amended by Act No. 19031), Enforcement Decree of the Specific Financial Information Act (Presidential Decree No. 33313), KoFIU Regulation on Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Ownership Verification, Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 5492), Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended, Articles 19 and 24-2) and Commercial Registration Act; under this framework the real-name registration of directors with the District Court Registry and the KoFIU UBO verification protocol operate together, with UBO data accessible to the Government of the Republic of Korea only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Extract of the Commercial Registry / Certificate of Registered Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization at the notary public office attached to the issuing district court, followed by a single Hague Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea when the receiving jurisdiction is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; where the receiving jurisdiction is a non-member state, the notarized certificate must be submitted for consular legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate of that state. The two authentication routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (current Certificate of Registered Matters confirming active status, no dissolution, no receivership and no liquidation, supplemented by a Certificate of Business Registration from the National Tax Service)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea and the National Tax Service (district tax office) of the head-office jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public, followed by either a Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Apostille Convention states or consular legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission in the destination state for non-member states; these two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the Korea-resident managing director and any foreign-address signatories for bank, tax and LC operations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of KR_YUHANGHOESA (Yuhan Hoesa), certified by the corporate secretary and notarized before a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: After notarization of the directors' signatures, the instrument is authenticated by a Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Convention member states, or by consular legalization at a Korean Embassy or Consulate for non-member states; never both in sequence, as the paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Certified Corporate Charter of the Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa KR_YUHANGHOESA, certified by the incorporating attorney and filed with the registering District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A notarized certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation is processed exclusively through the Hague Apostille procedure at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for member states, or exclusively through consular legalization at the competent Korean consulate for non-member states; chaining of apostille followed by consular legalization is strictly prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the corporate settlement relationship for SWIFT LC and irrevocable letter of credit operations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean foreign-exchange bank (commercial bank authorized under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act) maintaining the corporate settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank officer's signature on the reference letter is notarized and then either apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea if the receiving bank or authority is located in an Apostille Convention state, or legalized by the Korean consulate if located in a non-member state; the two alternatives are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Passport and Identity Documentation of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner and of the resident director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuance authority (resident registration office or the relevant foreign government) with certification by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized copies are authenticated by a single Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Convention states, or by consular legalization at the Korean mission in the issuing country for non-member states; these routes are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, signatories, counterparties, charterers and LC beneficiaries must be screened individually and continuously against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea's national sanctions measures administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information. Enhanced due diligence, including written corroboration of source of wealth and source of funds, is mandatory for every politically exposed person and for any person, entity or vessel connected to a sanctioned jurisdiction (including the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Iran, Syria, Cuba and the Crimea region). Because the ISIC 4669 wholesale petrochemical polymers trade is classified Medium Risk Enhanced, the complete customer due diligence file must be refreshed before every SWIFT or irrevocable LC transaction, and any name, country or vessel match must immediately suspend processing, escalate to the AML compliance officer, and, if unresolved within 24 hours, trigger a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: i-REGISTER (Internet Registry Office of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea) Trade Name Reservation and Search Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article 19 of the Korean Commercial Act, the trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be expressed in Korean script (Hangul); a purely Roman-alphabet name cannot be registered as the statutory corporate name, and the registered charter must also include the statutory designator 'Yuhan Hoesa' (the Korean statutory term for a limited liability company). Foreign corporate names are rendered in Hangul phonetic transliteration in the registered trade name; the original Latin or other-orthography name may be used only as an auxiliary trading name in commercial contracts and SWIFT/LC documentation. The four-tier naming test requires: (1) formal lexical distinctiveness from all existing trade names providing the same or similar business purpose within the same city, county or district; (2) phonetic distinctiveness of the Hangul transliteration when read aloud; (3) absence of any misrepresentation of nationality, public status, business scale or regulated activity; and (4) clearance of all prohibited and sensitive tokens requiring prior ministerial approval and of any name likely to mislead the public as to the nature of the entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry clerk rejects the proposed trade name, the applicant may, within two weeks of receiving the written rejection notice, file a written objection with the head of the competent District Court

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, particularly Articles 169, 287-2 through 287-40 governing the formation, registration and operation of a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company); Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 2-5; Registration of Commercial Enterprises Act, Article 10; and supporting Enforcement Decrees and Registration Rules thereunder.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court / Local District Court Registry Office under the Supreme Court of Korea Registration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Commercial Enterprise, together with the original notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital payment certificate, foreign-investment deposit certificate where applicable, and the pro-forma first board resolution minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act as an absolute minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Yuhan Hoesa. The only statutory condition is that the subscribed capital must have been actually paid in before commercial registration is applied for. For a foreign-invested entity, the foreign capital contribution must first be remitted into a blocked foreign-investment escrow account opened with a licensed foreign-exchange bank, and the funds are held under restriction until the incorporation registration certificate and business operator registration certificate are issued. The escrow release may be executed only by the directors expressly authorized in the first board resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION: Whereas the Company has been established as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, and whereas the subscription list and the capital contribution plan have been preliminarily approved by the organizers, and whereas the registration of the Company requires a formal first board resolution; Now, therefore, at the first meeting of the Board of Directors duly convened at the registered office, a quorum being present throughout, the directors adopt the following resolutions: 1. Subscription and Allotment of Share Capital. The subscription list is approved and ratified. The initial issued capital is fixed at KRW 100,000,000 divided into 10,000 shares of KRW 10,000 each, all of which are deemed fully subscribed by the founding shareholders whose names appear in the shareholders ledger before this meeting. The directors are directed to collect the full subscription moneys into the blocked escrow account opened with a licensed foreign exchange bank, and to execute the release instructions after the commercial registration certificate is issued. 2. Banking and Financial Authorization. The Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly, are authorized to open, maintain and close domestic and foreign currency bank accounts; to issue, endorse, accept, pay, and receive cheques, bills of exchange, and promissory notes; to sign letters of credit, documentary collections, and import-export settlement instructions; and to execute loan, foreign exchange, hedging, and guarantee agreements necessary for the purchase, shipment, storage and resale of petrochemical granules. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office is established at [street address], Seoul, Republic of Korea, and the Representative Director is authorized to file the adoption and any change in the office with the relevant Registry Office and the tax authority. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. [Name] is appointed a director and elected Representative Director with power to act individually; [Name] is appointed a director; [Name] is appointed statutory auditor under the Commercial Act; and [Name] is appointed Chief Compliance Officer. Each shall hold office until the first ordinary general meeting and may be re-appointed. 5. Corporate Governance and General Authorization. The Board approves the use of the official corporate seal, the adoption of a bank account signature card, and the engagement of Korean counsel to file the incorporation registration, business license, K-REACH notification and hazardous chemical warehouse licenses. All lawful acts performed by the organizers before this resolution are ratified and confirmed. There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned. This resolution is effective immediately. [Signed] Chairperson and Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Declaration and Opening of Blocked Capital Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA); Foreign Exchange Bank designated under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investor's declaration through KOTRA or the designated foreign-exchange bank before remitting capital from abroad. The declaration must include the foreign investor's identity and nationality, the amount and ratio of investment, the purpose clause covering wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules, and the proposed corporate name Yuhan Hoesa. The bank will open a temporary escrow account in the prospective company name and hold the remitted funds in blocked status until the Commercial Registry registration has been approved. Obtain the foreign-investment deposit certificate after remittance; this certificate must be quoted in the incorporation registration application.
required_dossiers: Passport or certificate of incorporation of foreign investor
Power of attorney authorizing local counsel
Memorandum to open escrow bank account
Proposed business plan and ISIC 4669 purpose statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is suspended or returned, supplement the certified translation of the foreign investor's charter and correct the business purpose wording to match ISIC 4669; resubmit within five business days to KOTRA or the same bank, and if the bank declines to open escrow, apply to another foreign-exchange bank with the provisional foreign investment report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public; external corporate counsel; founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage counsel to prepare the Articles of Incorporation under Commercial Act Articles 287-3 through 287-10. The Articles must set forth the corporate name, the precise purpose clause including import, export, wholesale storage and supply of petrochemical polymers, total authorized share capital, the initial paid-in capital, the number of issued shares, directors' rights, and audit provisions, as well as the registered address. Every incorporator must sign the Articles and appear before a Korean notary for signature attestation. Hold the first board meeting immediately after notarization, adopt the pro-forma board resolution, and have each director sign the minutes. Keep the notarial registration copy with escrow evidence for commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Passport and resident registration certificate of each incorporator
Consent of each proposed director and auditor
Registered office lease contract or owner consent
Minutes of the First Board of Directors Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses attestation on account of an inconsistent romanization or a defective purpose clause, amend the Articles and the internal governance schedules, then have all incorporators appear again; any alteration of capital or shareholders after signature requires a new notarial act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of Seoul Central District Court (or local District Court) under the Supreme Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate registration application form in the format prescribed by the Registration of Commercial Enterprises Act. Attach the notarized Articles, the first board resolution minutes, the escrow deposit certificate, the foreign investment declaration certificate, and consents from directors and auditor. The application must be filed with the district court having jurisdiction over the registered office. Pay the registration tax, local education surtax, and certificate fees at the court or revenue office. The registry will conduct a substantive legal examination and enter the company into the commercial register; after approval, request a corporate seal certificate and a certified corporate registration extract. Complete this filing within the statutory period after the notarial act.
required_dossiers: Consent forms of directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a cure notice for failure of documentation, cure the deficiencies and pay any assessed fees within ten days; if substantive issues remain, withdraw and refile after a corrective notarial act, and if the registry refuses registration, an immediate administrative appeal to the Supreme Court registry office is available under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Business License and Mandatory Social Insurance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (HomeTax system); district tax office; National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service; local employment and labor office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after the commercial registry has entered the company, apply for a business operator registration certificate under the Framework Act on National Taxes. The application must identify the main business as wholesale distribution of petrochemical polymers and include the registered office lease contract, the corporate registration excerpt, and expected annual sales. Upon approval, register for value-added tax, corporate income tax, payroll withholding, and electronic tax invoice issuance. Immediately after the tax registration, complete the mandatory registration for the employee National Pension, National Health Insurance, employment insurance and industrial accident compensation insurance with the respective insurers. For foreign-invested companies, file the certificate of paid-in capital with MOTIE to obtain the foreign investment confirmation.
required_dossiers: Certificate that the corporation registered with the Commercial Registry
Lease contract for the registered office
Insurance cover forms and employee list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS defers the business license, submit an actual-office confirmation letter from the building owner along with a rental payment statement; if an insurance registration is queried, make a retroactive commencement declaration and pay any overdue premiums in monthly installments to avoid administrative fines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: K-REACH Notification, Hazardous Chemicals Registration and Fire and Warehouse Safety Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Institute of Chemical Safety (Ministry of Environment); Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency; local fire and disaster prevention authority with jurisdiction over the warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess the imported virgin PE and PP granules against K-REACH and the Chemical Substances Control Act. Since the granules are chemical substances for trading, file a K-REACH substance notification or an exemption dossier with the National Institute of Chemical Safety using an Only Representative if the foreign manufacturer has none. Maintain a Korean-language Safety Data Sheet for every grade and lot. If storage of pellets is part of the wholesale operation, obtain the hazardous chemical handling registration and fire permit from the local fire station, install spill containment and dust control equipment, and have as-built drawings approved. Register the warehouse with KOSHA for occupational safety and prepare a chemical risk assessment, including ventilation, combustible dust control, and emergency response.
required_dossiers: Safety Data Sheets in Korean for each polymer grade
Structural load and racking design certificate
KOSHA workplace safety registration and risk assessment report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If K-REACH rejects the dossier for incomplete data, appoint an Only Representative and generate the missing hazard endpoints through the Korean chemical information search system; if the fire inspection fails, correct the facility, pay the re-inspection fee and pass the second inspection before any product sale from that storage location.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Environment - National Institute of Chemical Safety; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA); local municipal civil defense and fire prevention authority having jurisdiction over the warehouse.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Hazardous Chemicals Handling Permit or Registration under the Chemical Substances Control Act; K-REACH notification as importer or through an Only Representative; Fire Protection Facility Installation and Firefighting Certificate for warehouse storage; National Tax Service wholesale business operator registration carrying ISIC 4669.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment - Environmental Impact Assessment Administrative Office and local municipal environment division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA for a pure trading office with no physical storage; an Environmental Registration / pre-construction notification is required for a distribution warehouse larger than 500 square meters; a full statutory Environmental Impact Assessment Report is mandatory for storage facilities above 5,000 square meters or for any site located in or adjacent to water-source protection zones, conservation areas, or disaster-vulnerable zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater and stormwater run-off discharge from warehouse areas must not exceed BOD 60 mg/L, COD 70 mg/L, TSS 50 mg/L, T-N 20 mg/L, T-P 2 mg/L, and oil and grease 5 mg/L. Fugitive volatile organic compounds at the site boundary must not exceed 100 ppm as carbon as a 10-minute average; resin transfer and ventilation exhaust must use a vapor control or filtration device achieving at least 95 percent capture-control efficiency. Contaminated polymer, off-spec granules, spill cleanup materials, or residual solvents, if hazardous, must be stored in double-walled labeled containers and removed within 30 days by a licensed hazardous waste transporter under the Wastes Control Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense and Fire Safety Certificate from the National Fire Agency and the local fire-fighting authority; structural and racking load inspection certificate under Korean Design Standard KDS 41 61 00 for racks exceeding 3.6 meters or stacking heights above 9 meters; KOSHA workplace approval covering combustible dust risk assessment, emergency response, protective equipment, and chemical hazard communication; and a district civil defense disaster impact confirmation for any warehouse exceeding 1,000 square meters.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with electronic filing and registration via the HomeTax portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr); border and customs tax operations are administered by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS portal (https://unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) engaged in bulk petrochemical polymer wholesale distribution: (1) Prepare the entity's foreign investor ownership documents, articles of incorporation, domestic lease evidence for the principal place of business, and representative identity documents; no statutory paid-in minimum capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa. (2) Submit the business registration application to the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business, either in person or through HomeTax, before commencing taxable business operations. (3) The NTS will issue the Korean Business Registration Certificate, which contains the 10-digit Business Registration Number; this number serves simultaneously as the national TIN and the VAT identification number for the LLC. (4) If the foreign parent has no Korean permanent establishment and is itself acting as a non-resident supplier of goods or services into Korea, the non-resident entity must appoint a domestic tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes and apply through the jurisdictional district tax office for a non-resident business and VAT registration number; this is a separate TIN from the local LLC's number. (5) Where cross-border trading is performed, the LLC must also register with the Korea Customs Service in UNI-PASS to obtain a customs clearance business identification number for import and export declarations. (6) The LLC must file VAT returns electronically through HomeTax and issue electronic tax invoices in the NTS e-invoice system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC is classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is subject to entity-level corporate tax on worldwide income; it is not treated as a pass-through entity. Foreign shareholders are separately taxable on dividends or remittances, and the local LLC remains the registered taxpayer for corporate and VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification; Korea does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC. There are no optional hybrid mismatch entity classification elections under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, and anti-hybrid rules apply. Only general Korean tax elections are available, such as VAT simplified taxable status for eligible small businesses below KRW 80 million annual turnover, which is not applicable to an institutional petrochemical wholesale enterprise.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea; for cross-border import and export clearances, the Korea Customs Service administers customs VAT under the Customs Act using the same 10% headline rate on taxable importation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No KRW threshold: registration is mandatory upon commencement of taxable business activity in Korea. A local Yuhan Hoesa with a Korean place of business has VAT nexus and must obtain a Business Registration Number. The simplified taxable regime is available only for eligible small businesses with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80 million and is not consistent with bulk petrochemical wholesale trading; therefore the general VAT registration and invoicing regime applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registered general VAT taxpayers must issue and transmit electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice system for all business-to-business taxable supplies. Each electronic tax invoice must contain the supplier and customer business registration numbers, supply value, VAT amount, and item description, and must be submitted to the NTS within the statutory e-invoice transmission deadlines. Korea does not operate a continuous transaction control or real-time fiscal clearance and digital stamping regime comparable to Latin American or Southern European models; instead, the NTS receives e-invoice data in near real time and reconciles it against VAT returns and Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export and import declarations. For exports, the electronic tax invoice is issued at zero rate, and customs export declaration data provides the clearance evidence. Import VAT is assessed and collected by the Korea Customs Service at the border at 10% and is recoverable as input VAT by the registered LLC subject to ordinary input tax requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export supplies of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules qualify for zero-rated VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act if the goods are actually exported under a valid export declaration filed with the Korea Customs Service, title and risk pass to a non-resident purchaser, the goods depart Korea, the sale is supported by commercial documentation, and export proceeds are received in foreign exchange and repatriated to Korea in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The zero-rated treatment also entitles the registered exporter to claim a quick refund of remaining input VAT credits attributable to zero-rated export sales through the VAT return. For this ISIC 4669 wholesale goods transaction, physical customs clearance is the core zero-rating evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Outward Clearance / Export Bill of Entry) approved by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading (ocean carriage) or Air Waybill evidencing export movement out of Korea
Commercial invoice issued to the foreign buyer describing the bulk petrochemical polymers and the agreed Incoterms
Packing list and vessel or containerized shipment loading records
Sales contract or purchase order between the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and the non-resident purchaser
Electronic tax invoice issued at zero rate through the NTS electronic tax invoice system

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Acquisition Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, confirming receipt of foreign currency export proceeds within the statutory repatriation period
UNI-PASS export clearance data report or Korea Customs Service-issued export confirmation statement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service will scrutinize the customs export declaration, transport documents, electronic tax invoice, and foreign exchange receipt evidence to verify that the goods left Korea and that proceeds were repatriated. If zero-rating is claimed without genuine physical export, with false documentation, or where export proceeds are not received within the 180-day foreign-exchange settlement period, the NTS may disallow the zero rate and reassess output VAT at 10% on the supply value, together with statutory interest and additional tax for false tax invoices and failure of electronic invoice obligations under the Value-Added Tax Act. Fraudulent cases may be referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Retrospective clawback may reach all open tax years under the Framework Act on National Taxes, with the assessment limitation period extended for false or fraudulent returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) exercising foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised current account with full convertibility for trade-related settlement, but capital account transactions remain subject to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its subordinate regulations. For the subject entity engaged in wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules, import payments for physical polymer cargoes are classified as current account transactions requiring only a genuine underlying trade contract and standard bank documentation. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are likewise treated as current account items for dividends, but the bank will require evidence of corporate tax clearance, audited financial statements, and a dividend resolution; remittance is generally permitted without prior central bank approval, yet the paying Korean bank must file an investment registration certificate and monitor the transaction under its internal anti-money laundering policy. Capital account inflows such as foreign parent loans and equity injections require a preliminary declaration of acquisition or loan agreement on the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) through a designated foreign exchange bank. Convertibility of the Korean won is broadly achievable, but currency mismatches can arise because polymer trading contracts are often invoiced in US dollars while local operating costs are incurred in KRW. Since Korea applies a real demand principle for FX forwards, the entity must demonstrate a firm underlying trade transaction to hedge this mismatch. Surrender obligations were substantially liberalised, so export receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts, but collection must occur within the statutory settlement period. In practical underwriting, the bank will review trade flow consistency, invoice authenticity, bill of lading dates, and payment matching to distinguish genuine trade operations from disguised capital movements. The absence of any surrender ratio lowers friction, but strict reporting under FEIS remains mandatory for each trade transaction. Overall, South Korea offers high FX flexibility for operating cash flow, with only narrow regulatory barriers around capital account declarations, non-resident borrowing, and speculative FX positions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected and settled within six months from the date of export declaration, unless an extension is separately approved by the Minister of Economy and Finance or delegated to the Bank of Korea; there is no mandatory conversion ratio into Korean won, and proceeds may be held in a domestic foreign currency account at a foreign exchange bank, but all receipts must be reported to the foreign exchange bank and traceable to the underlying export customs clearance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account with foreign currency sub-ledger for import LC payments
Basic Operational Currency Account and Export Proceeds Receivable Account
Capital Escrow Account for FDI verification and KRW operational account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very Low - the Financial Services Commission and the Bank of Korea do not recognise offshore fintech EMI or electronic money institutions as licensed banks for corporate cross-border settlement. A foreign EMI cannot open a regulated KRW account or execute FX declarations under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Using such an entity for petrochemical trade settlements would create severe regulatory risk and likely lead to frozen funds, blocked FEIS reporting, and bank rejection of the underlying transactions. The only compliant approach is to use a traditional Korean commercial bank or a locally licensed digital bank chartered under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and even then the digital institution would need support for LC operations and trade-based AML screening, which most Korean digital-only banks do not provide.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident corporate client in a medium-risk enhanced review class, Korean commercial banks generally require a physical in-branch interview with the statutory director or a duly empowered representative and at least one controlling beneficial owner. Remote consular notarisation and apostilled corporate documents may support pre-approval screening, but the final onboarding decision is in practice conditional on an in-person appearance at the designated branch in Seoul or Busan. In exceptional cases, a bank officer may accept a video-call interview followed by a physical visit from the local representative certified under a registered power of attorney, but most tier-1 banks retain the mandate for at least one physical appearance to satisfy the anti-money laundering requirement to identify the customer in person.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Members' Meeting and approval of audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's statutory records at registered office; no court filing for a Yuhan Hoesa unless a registration amendment is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; by 31 March for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are liable to administrative fines up to KRW 2 million for non-convening; failure to approve accounts prevents tax carry-forwards and may trigger NTS estimated assessment; persistent default may lead to court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (self-assessment) under the Corporate Income Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; by 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year; one-month extension to 30 April available for audited entities or with NTS approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled return attracts a 20% additional tax (40% for fraudulent omission) plus daily overdue interest at the statutory rate; criminal prosecution may impose imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to KRW 20 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return (10% of national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of principal place of business through WeTax local tax e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as national corporate income tax return, within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers non-declaration penalties and monthly late payment surcharges; persistent non-payment may result in business registration strike-off and forced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report filing to the Financial Supervisory Service (when audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; by 31 March for a calendar-year company and before the annual members' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the audit report is subject to regulatory fines, suspension of accounting firm approval, and criminal referral under the Act on External Audit; false statements may also expose directors to fraud liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise status report (applicable where non-resident members hold interests)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through a designated foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June for the preceding calendar year; changes in ownership within 30 days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting may incur an administrative fine up to KRW 5 million, cancellation of foreign investment registration, and loss of statutory tax incentive benefits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a certified independent audit is compulsory if the Yuhan Hoesa meets any of the following: (1) balance-sheet total assets at the prior fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.2 million); (2) annual turnover exceeds KRW 20 billion (approx. USD 15.4 million) and the average number of regular employees is at least 300; (3) the company is a parent or subsidiary in a group whose consolidated assets exceed KRW 5 trillion (approx. USD 3.8 billion); or (4) the Financial Services Commission designates the company as a public-interest or SEC-registered-like entity for audit. These thresholds are reassessed every fiscal year and are adjusted by Presidential Decree.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Applicable standards are K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for entities required to file consolidated or public-interest accounts; otherwise Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) for non-public companies. A wholesale petrochemical trading company is subject to K-IFRS 15 on revenue, K-IFRS 9 on financial assets/instruments and foreign exchange LC obligations, K-IFRS 2 on inventory measurement (or K-GAAP equivalents).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each fiscal year, the LLC must collect written confirmation of its beneficial owners (title, nationality, address, and percentage holding) by 31 March. Any transfer of membership quotas must be registered with the Korean Commercial Registry within 14 days, and a report of any foreign investor ownership change must be filed with the designated foreign-exchange bank and NTS within 30 days. The company must retain all UBO records for at least 7 years and update the internal register upon any change in control or ownership.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 5,000 per annum for a licensed corporate service provider in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 per annum for a certified K-IFRS audit of a petrochemical wholesale trading LLC with typical inventory and LC activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea's Corporate Income Tax Act provides progressive rates of 9% on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income, 19% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion, and 21% on income between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion, with a top headline rate of 24% above KRW 300 billion; however, including the 10% local income tax surtax, the combined statutory headline CIT rate is effectively 25% for income exceeding KRW 300 billion. For a wholesale petrochemical trading LLC, no general free-zone patent box or R&D super-deduction applies, but the entity may claim ordinary business expense deductions, bad debt reserves under the Framework Act on Taxation, and the Small and Medium Enterprise tax credit if qualified.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean corporate income tax return: Form No. 1 (Business Income Return) for domestic corporations under the Corporate Income Tax Act, filed via HomeTax System (HTS) at www.hometax.go.kr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year (by March 31 for a calendar-year corporation); a one-month automatic extension is available if the financial statements are audited by a tax attorney or certified public accountant, making the extended deadline April 30.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and corporate registry information (business registration number, legal entity name, representative director, registered address, tax office jurisdiction).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean business registration number exactly as issued to the Yuhan Hoesa. The foreign parent or ultimate beneficial owner must be disclosed in the supplementary shareholder information schedule if non-resident ownership exceeds 5%, and a Korean resident representative director or tax agent must be identified for service of process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year and accounting period (beginning date and ending date of the tax year).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly formed or newly acquired Korean LLC, enter the actual commencement date of business. If the entity elected a non-calendar fiscal year, secure advance approval from the National Tax Service (NTS) and ensure the reporting period does not exceed 12 months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classification of corporation and tax computation method (general corporation, holding company, small or medium enterprise, or foreign investment company).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Yuhan Hoesa is a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, mark the appropriate foreign-investment enterprise code and attach the foreign investment report certificate. Do not mark 'domestic small corporation' unless the Korean entity independently satisfies the SME size standards under the Framework Act on SMEs, regardless of foreign parent size.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of financial position items: total assets, total liabilities, and capital stock as of the fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident owned LLCs, maintain separate books under Korean GAAP or K-IFRS. Cross-border intercompany account balances, including payables to the foreign parent for bulk polymer inventory, must be included at arm's-length values; any interest-free or disguised loan may be recharacterized by the NTS as constructive dividend or taxable interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement items: gross revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, selling and administrative expenses, operating income, non-operating income, non-operating expenses, and pre-tax net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide-sourced income allocable to the Korean permanent establishment. For a wholesale trading LLC, rigorously document title passage, Incoterms, and inventory risk. The NTS will reclassify trading income as Korean-source if the sales solicitation, negotiation, or contract conclusion occurs in Korea, even if the client is a foreign related party.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between book income and tax-adjusted taxable income: add-backs of non-deductible expenses, deductible reserve additions, and subtraction of non-taxable income or tax-exempt dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Flag any payments to the foreign parent for royalties, management fees, or interest. Under Article 93 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and domestic transfer pricing rules, non-arm's-length payments are disallowed. Entertainments, donations, and client hospitality above statutory thresholds are non-deductible; failing to add back these items creates an abnormal tax deficiency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income, corporate income tax at progressive rates, and additional local income tax (10% of CIT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate CIT using the statutory brackets and compute the local income tax surtax as 10% of the CIT amount on the same tax base. Non-resident shareholders cannot directly credit Korean local income tax in their home jurisdiction unless the applicable DTA grants credit for local surtax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, including foreign tax credits, early payment credits, employment tax credits, and SME investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a wholesale distributor, only claim credits substantiated by Korean statutory requirements. A foreign tax credit is available only for foreign taxes paid on Korean-source income by the Korean entity, not for taxes payable by foreign shareholders on dividends received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable after credits, prior-year assessments, installment payments, and final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before remitting any final tax payment, verify whether the transaction with the foreign parent involves a permanent establishment risk of the foreign parent in Korea. If the NTS deems the Korean subsidiary to be a dependent agent PE, additional branch-level tax and withholding obligations arise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director, preparer, and tax agent signatures and declaration of completeness.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean representative director must sign the return. A foreign director cannot rely on a power of attorney to avoid personal certification. The tax agent, if any, must also co-sign and bear joint liability for fraudulent misstatements under the Framework Act on Taxpayer Rights.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax if filed within one month of the statutory due date, increasing to 20% plus an additional 1.2% per month (or 30% per year) for continued non-payment; where the tax authority makes a no-return determination, the additional tax is 0.75% of the deficient tax for every day of delay, up to 75%. Failure to submit attached financial statements, shareholder schedules, or transfer pricing documentation triggers a per-document penalty of up to KRW 30 million under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act. Intentional omission or false reporting exposes the entity to criminal tax fraud charges under Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 2 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% dividend withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax on the dividend WHT base) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, reduced to 15% or less to 0% depending on the applicable double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for reduced withholding under the Korea-OECD DTA network, the non-resident shareholder or creditor must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, issued for the relevant fiscal year and stating residence for treaty purposes; (2) provide a Korean-standard Beneficial Ownership Certificate (Form 6-2 or NTS-provided form) declaring the recipient is the actual owner and not a conduit or agent; (3) submit the TRC and beneficial ownership declarations to the Korean paying entity before making the remittance; and (4) file a withholding tax return through HomeTax to report the payment and claim the treaty rate. The NTS will deny treaty relief and impose the 22% statutory withholding plus penalties if the documentation is incomplete or the NTS determines the recipient lacks substance and merely channels funds to a third-country ultimate parent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For royalties on intellectual property or know-how, the statutory Korean WHT is 22% (20% plus 2% local surtax), generally reduced to 10% under most OECD DTAs where the recipient is the beneficial owner. For interest on intercompany loans, the statutory WHT is likewise 22%, generally reduced to 10% under most DTAs, provided the lender is not an agent, nominee, or financing conduit. Domestic Korean borrowing from a foreign controlling shareholder is also subject to the thin capitalization rule limiting deductible interest to 3 times the equity investment (or 6 times for financial institutions); the disallowed interest is recharacterized as a constructive dividend subject to 22% withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File preparation and submission is required for a multinational enterprise group with annual consolidated revenue of KRW 100 billion or more; a Local File is required for the Korean entity when its intercompany transactions in the relevant category reach KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year, and a Country-by-Country Report is required when the group's consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion. Even below these thresholds, contemporaneous TP documentation is mandatory if the NTS issues an adjustment or requests evidence of arm's-length pricing.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies the OECD arm's-length principle and allows the NTS to recharacterize transactions conducted by a Korean entity that lacks economic substance, including circular transactions, shell companies, and excessive management fee arrangements. Although Korea has separate Economic Substance Regulations only for special-purpose entities in tax-haven jurisdictions under the International Tax Adjustment Act, a wholesale LLC with substantial inventory trading must evidence substance through local employees, offices, contracts, and CIGA functions; failing this may expose the entity to permanent establishment attribution adjustments and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting bulk petrochemical sales revenue, fabricating invoice dates, or using a related offshore procurement vehicle to divert Korean-source profits without filing under the Corporate Income Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, conviction carries imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of up to 2 times the evaded tax; additionally, the NTS imposes a 40% negligence penalty plus a 20% understatement penalty and daily late-payment surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Repeat offenders face aggravated imprisonment of up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts will pierce the corporate veil if the director uses the LLC as a sham to evade taxes, commingles assets, or strips profits to foreign shell entities. The director is personally liable for the full amount of unpaid tax, and under Article 10(2) of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, a responsible director can be sentenced to imprisonment of up to 5 years; the foreign parent's director may also be held personally liable if the Korean LLC is found to be an alter ego.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Shell Company Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a low-function, high-risk distributor that passes more than 85% of its gross profit to the foreign parent through excessive royalties, service fees, or advance pricing imbalances without any real employees, inventory risk, or decision-making functions in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may reassess taxable income under Articles 4 and 5 of the Adjustment of International Taxes Act using the TNMM or profit split, impose a 20% adjustment penalty on the additional tax, and disallow all excessive fees. Failure to submit the Local File within the statutory 60-day request window triggers a penalty of up to KRW 30 million per document, and the denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test exposes the transaction to full 22% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the principle of substance-over-form and the doctrine of serious negligence, a Korean resident director who signs the return without performing due diligence on the intercompany pricing is jointly liable for the CIT deficiency plus penalties; where the director intentionally structured the shell to divert profits, criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion can result in imprisonment up to 3 years and a travel ban or blacklisting by the NTS preventing departure from Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Cross-Border Remittance Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident parent without withholding, or fabricating a TRC and beneficial ownership declaration to obtain a reduced DTA rate for a recipient that is a mere conduit in a zero-tax jurisdiction without substantive activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 11 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and Article 30 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the payer remains liable for the withheld amount plus a 10% penalty for failure to withhold, plus 0.75% per month on the unpaid withholding until payment. Falsification of treaty documents constitutes document forgery and tax fraud, leading to fines up to KRW 200 million and imprisonment up to 7 years under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act and the Criminal Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signs the remittance instruction or approves the false withholding return is personally and criminally liable for the unpaid withholding tax and may be subject to a travel ban, passport revocation, and asset seizure by the NTS. In egregious cases, the Korean court may order personal restitution to the NTS of the full grossed-up dividend amount and impose imprisonment of up to 5 years; the director is also disqualified from serving as a company officer in Korea.
